title: Mercury SupplyChain — Inference Intake & Call Scratchpad
content:
Context: Mercury SupplyChain (small-to-mid logistics SaaS) is exploring an LLM-powered routing assistant for customer support and internal dispatch triage. They want a low-latency hosted or private option for US customers; tight cost targets (<= $0.0009/token effective) and bursty peak windows with very strict 200ms per-token tail requirements for chat flows.

Quick call notes (2025-09-18 kickoff, 11:00 PT)
- Attendees: Clara Huang (Mercury PM), Rajesh Iyer (Mercury infra lead), Sam (ops), Aisha (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood solutions)
- High level ask: replace current rule-based triage with LLM -> extract intent + recommended SLA routing + suggested dispatch steps. Start with hosted API PoC, then evaluate Dedicated or Private depending on latency and data residency.
- Traffic estimate: 8k daily active users, average 2.6 requests/user/day, median prompt length ~220 tokens, median response ~90 tokens, with 5x spikes during morning rollout windows.
- SLOs: 95th percentile < 300ms latency (end-to-end for short chat replies), 200ms per-token streaming requirement for interactive agent UI.
- Cost goal: keep per-interaction cost below $0.10 for median case; long-term target <= $0.06 when optimized.

Notes on technical constraints (from Rajesh)
- Data residency: initial dataset can be processed in Redwood hosted US clusters; later need VPC-only processing for PHI-adjacent metadata (customer phone/email).
- KMS: Mercury uses AWS KMS CMKs in us-east-1 for secrets; want Redwood to support CMEK for Private option.
- Network: inbound webhook traffic originates from customer's on-prem webhook gateway; prefer mutual-TLS option for webhook origin verification.

Initial recommended architecture (brainstorm)
- Phase 0: Hosted API PoC using a 7B open model in Redwood catalog tuned for conversational routing. Use prefix KV caching for common customer queries and standard intro templates to reduce token budget.
- Phase 1: If latency or residency issues appear, move to Dedicated (reserved GPUs) in us-east-1 with pinned model version and canary rollout rules.
- Phase 2: Private VPC deployment (air-gapped option) where all inference occurs on customer VPC with Redwood control plane in a separate admin network. CMEK + syslogs forwarded to their SIEM.

Performance/implementation assumptions to validate quickly
- Model selection: baseline 7B int8 -> measure latency/cost; compare to 13B quantized variant for tail-latency and quality tradeoff.
- Batch settings: continuous batching with max batch=8, target latency budget=120ms; explore micro-batching for spikes.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for templates and most common utterances (should save ~22% token cost based on similar pilots). Need ability to pre-warm cache on deploy/rollout.

Gotchas and red flags (from call + follow-ups)
- Their web frontend expects streaming tokens within 150ms of request start; many models will not meet that in hosted mode without dedicated capacity and pre-warmed KV state.
- Spike patterns are highly correlated (morning windows) causing queueing: autoscaling must be aggressive; need burst pool or overprovision window to avoid tail blowouts.
- They want strict redaction: user-uploaded notes sometimes contain PII; need deterministic redaction prior to sending to hosted model or require Private.
- Cost target tightness: current per-token unit costs may require combining caching + 7B quantization + output length control to hit $0.0009/token effective.
- Monitoring hooks: Mercury wants token-level attribution to customer features (route id, support tier) and prompt hashing for quality regression alerts. Ensure Redwood Console will show these granularity.

Open questions to resolve (priority ordering)
1) Can Redwood hosted meet their per-token streaming tail without Dedicated? (ask infra team to run a 7B streaming latency sim with real prompt distribution)
2) CMEK availability timeline for Private deployments and any additional compliance docs required.
3) Pre-warm / cache seeding API: Mercury wants a way to push a list of 2k common templates to KV store before going live.
4) Does Redwood support mutual-TLS webhooks or an alternate signed-request scheme?
5) Autoscale burst options and dedicated burst pool pricing/commit model for short high-surge windows.

Immediate next steps / action items
- Aisha: run a quick perf sim with Redwood hosted 7B (example prompts attached in repo link) and produce 95/99 latencies for streaming tail by 2025-09-26. (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mercury-poc)
- Diego: create a terse one-pager on KV seeding options and estimated token savings; share by 2025-09-22.
- Rajesh (Mercury): share sample prompt corpus (anonymized) and peak schedule (CSV) by 2025-09-23.
- Clara (Mercury): confirm compliance floor (is PHI expected?) and whether phone numbers must be deterministically redacted before sending to hosted system.
- Follow-up meeting: week of 2025-09-29 to review perf sim and decide Dedicated trial threshold.

Manual notes / scratch ideas
- Consider using structured function-calls for routing output instead of free text to reduce token churn and make downstream deterministic (helps cost + parsing).
- Try 1-token response anchors where agent can return a short intent code + small human-readable message; then fetch long-form templates only when needed.
- Explore session-level KV vs request-level KV for customer-specific context; session-level could improve tail for repeated customers.

Snippets / quick config sketch (for SE handoff)
- Model: rwd-open-7b-int8 (baseline)
- Streaming: enabled, chunk_ms target 60ms, initial chunk size target 3 tokens
- Batching: continuous, max_batch=8, batch_timeout=12ms, adaptive=true
- KV cache: prefix:true, store:ephemeral by default, allow preseed:true
- Rollouts: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with autoscale warmup 10m

Quick risk summary for sales / CS
- If Mercury insists on <150ms streaming tail, likely need Dedicated or early Private. That increases initial cost but makes SLA feasible.
- Data residency / redaction requirements could force Private deployment which adds onboarding friction + longer lead time.
- Cost target is achievable but will require multiple optimizations and aggressive monitoring.

Notes to self (style + follow-up)
- Keep momentum: small wins and perf numbers matter; show 2-3 cost reduction levers (cache, quantize, function-calls) with measured impact.
- When sharing perf sim, include raw prompt/response histograms and a short note on what we controlled in the sim (batching, warm cache or not).

End scratchpad. More as we get corpus and run sims.
